news.full_article_text: SC castigates Centre over medicine overpricing, asks 'can you justify this loot' New Delhi, Flagging the "massive difference" between the MRP of medicines and the price to retailers, the Supreme Court on Tuesday slammed the Centre asking if it can provide "any justification for this loot" and also if manufacturers be allowed to "run amok". A bench of justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta observed that the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority seems to be a "totally defunct" body and asked the government why the entire system was working to help pharmaceutical manufacturers. The top court reserved its verdict on two petitions which raised drug-related issues, including that of ensuring strict price control over medicines. Deep Dive After the Centre told the bench about the decision to cap the trade margin on anti-cancer drugs at 30 per cent of the maximum retail price , the bench asked why there can't be a uniform 16 per cent margin on all medicines. "The government policy is that entire ecosystem is not to be controlled," Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Centre, told the bench. The bench observed that a medicine having ₹ 15 as price to retailer , carries an MRP of ₹ 250. "Can you show any justification for this loot," the bench asked, adding, "The government is allowing this to happen. It is under the government's own eyes that it is happening." When Bhati referred to the aspect of having control, the bench asked, "Should it be allowed to run amok?" The law officer told the bench that medicine prices in India were among the lowest in the world. While referring to the difference between the MRP and PTR, the bench said, "Why is the entire system working to help these people ." The top court referred to a recent case where a medical distributor's wife was admitted to a hospital for cancer treatment. It said the hospital charged ₹ 1.30 lakh for an injection which was available at a price of ₹ 11,000 to the distributor. "It seems that the public at large is living in some day dream that some day they will be benefitted by the NPPA," the bench observed. NPPA was constituted as an independent regulator for pricing of drugs and to ensure availability and accessibility of medicines at affordable prices. When Bhati referred to the issue of control, the bench observed, "It is not a question of control. There is 300 per cent, 400 per cent or more difference. Why this difference? Where does that difference go? What is the justification for this massive difference." The law officer referred to the Centre's affidavit which said the Indian drug market is fairly competitive, with a large number of pharmaceutical companies in every drug segment, resulting in one of the lowest prices in the world. When Bhati stressed on the need for a calibrated approach, the bench observed that patients don't have the bargaining powers and they have to shell out exorbitant price for medicines. "We wish every medicine is considered as generic medicine," the bench said. It also questioned the Centre why it took so long to cap the trade margin on anti-cancer drugs at 30 per cent of the MRP. "Only after we started putting questions, the government has woken up and now you are saying we have done this," the bench told the law officer. Bhati also referred to the aspect of growth of the pharmaceutical industry. "You are talking about commerce and economic policy. Don't weigh patients against commerce," the bench said. "When we talk of patients and their lives, can we look at it with a capitalist view?," it asked. While hearing the matter on October 12, the top court had said the Centre's response on capping the trade margin of anti-cancer drugs at 30 per cent of the MRP was "hardly anything to be happy about" and questioned why the government cannot cap trade margins of other medicines. The Centre, which had earlier come under severe criticism from the top court for steep markup of cancer drugs by hospitals, said that the government has taken an important decision to cap the trade margin on anti-cancer drugs at 30 per cent of the MRP, which is expected to result in annual savings of approximately ₹ 2,500 crore to patients. The bench had said that the Centre's response was insufficient and flagged that a single saline drip was sold in market for ₹ 270 while its actual cost was ₹ 11. One of the petitions sought a direction to the authorities to make drug formulations more cost-effective by preventing alleged unethical overpricing of essential medicines by pharma companies and retailers. It also sought directions to ensure strict price control under the Drugs Order, 2013, to prevent violations of the price-fixing mechanism in the drug supply chain and disproportionate profit-making by retailers through unfair trade practices. The other plea has sought disciplinary action against medical practitioners for not prescribing generic medicines to patients. news.story_lead: Cyclone Arnab starts landfall process along Andhra Pradesh coast, triggers heavy rain and strong winds Authorities remain on high alert as rescue and relief teams continue to take precautionary measures to minimise the impact of the severe cyclonic storm. Cyclone Arnab's landfall process started along the Andhra Pradesh coast on Wednesday around 1:10am, bringing strong winds and heavy rainfall to several areas, the Indian Meteorological Department said. In its bulletin issued at 1.10am on October 28, the IMD said Arnab’ was moving westwards over the west central Bay of Bengal, close to the Andhra Pradesh coast and Yanam, at a speed of 10 kmph.
news.full_article_text: Cyclone Arnab starts landfall process along Andhra Pradesh coast, triggers heavy rain and strong winds Authorities remain on high alert as rescue and relief teams continue to take precautionary measures to minimise the impact of the severe cyclonic storm. Cyclone Arnab's landfall process started along the Andhra Pradesh coast on Wednesday around 1:10am, bringing strong winds and heavy rainfall to several areas, the Indian Meteorological Department said. In its bulletin issued at 1.10am on October 28, the IMD said Arnab’ was moving westwards over the west central Bay of Bengal, close to the Andhra Pradesh coast and Yanam, at a speed of 10 kmph. IMD estimated the storm’s intensity at 125-135 kmph, with gusts reaching 150 kmph. The storm is expected to cross the coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam , south of Yanam, between 2 am and 4 am. Winds are likely to gradually weaken after landfall. Track live updates on Cyclone Arnab Authorities remain on high alert as rescue and relief teams continue to monitor the situation and take precautionary measures to minimise the impact of the severe cyclonic storm. Andhra Pradesh and Odisha had stepped up preparations on Tuesday ahead of the expected landfall of very severe cyclonic storm Arnab, with thousands of people moved to safety, nearly 4,000 cyclone shelters readied and at least 50 trains cancelled across the region. Air travel impacted Air travel was also affected, with at least 21 flights cancelled at Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam airports on Tuesday. The cancellations affected services to Chennai, Bengaluru, Visakhapatnam and Kadapa. An official said 15 flights scheduled to operate from Vijayawada airport on Wednesday had also been cancelled. Also read: Cyclone Arnab: Why Bay of Bengal storms tend to form after the monsoon Andhra Pradesh ensures preparedness The Andhra Pradesh government had arranged 2,131 cyclone shelters across 20 districts and placed 1,087 medical teams on standby in areas likely to be affected. Officials said 8,281 emergency beds and 1,274 ambulances had also been made available. Deep Dive Authorities had moved people out of vulnerable areas and shifted 1,351 pregnant women to hospitals. The government had stocked two months' worth of essential commodities at 14,686 ration shops, while cyclone alerts had been sent to the mobile phones of 2.70 crore people. Railways monitored 600 km of tracks, cancelled services The South Coast Railway had cancelled 24 trains scheduled for Wednesday, while the East Coast Railway had cancelled 22. The South Eastern Railway had also cancelled four trains, officials said. IMD director general Mrunjay Mohapatra had warned of potentially damaging winds along the coast. Odisha had moved over 30,000 people to cyclone shelters Odisha had intensified its preparations, with heavy rain already reported in parts of the state. Schools had been closed in 16 of its 30 districts, while more than 30,000 people had been moved to cyclone shelters against a target of 48,000, a revenue department official said. Entry to sea beaches had been prohibited. Special Relief Commissioner (SRC) Rajesh P Patil said 135 permanent cyclone shelters and around 1,600 temporary shelters had been prepared to accommodate people from vulnerable areas. Jharkhand had shut schools, issued yellow alert In neighbouring Jharkhand, the Ranchi district administration had ordered schools to remain closed on October 28 and 29 as authorities prepared for adverse weather. A yellow alert for heavy rain had been issued for Ranchi, Khunti, Simdega, Gumla, Lohardaga, Saraikela-Kharsawan, East Singhbhum and West Singhbhum for 24 hours from 8.30 am on October 28. prelims_facts: Cyclone Arnab starts landfall process along Andhra Pradesh coast, triggers heavy rain and strong winds
Authorities remain on high alert as rescue and relief teams continue to take precautionary measures to minimise the impact of the severe cyclonic storm.

Cyclone Arnab's landfall process started along the Andhra Pradesh coast on Wednesday around 1:10am, bringing strong winds and heavy rainfall to several areas, the Indian Meteorological Department said.
In its bulletin issued at 1.10am on October 28, the IMD said Arnab’ was moving westwards over the west central Bay of Bengal, close to the Andhra Pradesh coast and Yanam, at a speed of 10 kmph.
IMD estimated the storm’s intensity at 125-135 kmph, with gusts reaching 150 kmph.
The storm is expected to cross the coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam , south of Yanam, between 2 am and 4 am. Winds are likely to gradually weaken after landfall.

Track live updates on Cyclone Arnab Authorities remain on high alert as rescue and relief teams continue to monitor the situation and take precautionary measures to minimise the impact of the severe cyclonic storm. Andhra Pradesh and Odisha had stepped up preparations on Tuesday ahead of the expected landfall of very severe cyclonic storm Arnab, with thousands of people moved to safety, nearly 4,000 cyclone shelters readied and at least 50 trains cancelled across the region. Air travel impacted Air travel was also affected, with at least 21 flights cancelled at Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam airports on Tuesday. The cancellations affected services to Chennai, Bengaluru, Visakhapatnam and Kadapa. An official said 15 flights scheduled to operate from Vijayawada airport on Wednesday had also been cancelled. Also read: Cyclone Arnab: Why Bay of Bengal storms tend to form after the monsoon Andhra Pradesh ensures preparedness The Andhra Pradesh government had arranged 2,131 cyclone shelters across 20 districts and placed 1,087 medical teams on standby in areas likely to be affected. Officials said 8,281 emergency beds and 1,274 ambulances had also been made available. Deep Dive Authorities had moved people out of vulnerable areas and shifted 1,351 pregnant women to hospitals. The government had stocked two months' worth of essential commodities at 14,686 ration shops, while cyclone alerts had been sent to the mobile phones of 2.70 crore people. Railways monitored 600 km of tracks, cancelled services The South Coast Railway had cancelled 24 trains scheduled for Wednesday, while the East Coast Railway had cancelled 22. The South Eastern Railway had also cancelled four trains, officials said. IMD director general Mrunjay Mohapatra had warned of potentially damaging winds along the coast. Odisha had moved over 30,000 people to cyclone shelters Odisha had intensified its preparations, with heavy rain already reported in parts of the state. Schools had been closed in 16 of its 30 districts, while more than 30,000 people had been moved to cyclone shelters against a target of 48,000, a revenue department official said. Entry to sea beaches had been prohibited. Special Relief Commissioner (SRC) Rajesh P Patil said 135 permanent cyclone shelters and around 1,600 temporary shelters had been prepared to accommodate people from vulnerable areas. Jharkhand had shut schools, issued yellow alert In neighbouring Jharkhand, the Ranchi district administration had ordered schools to remain closed on October 28 and 29 as authorities prepared for adverse weather. A yellow alert for heavy rain had been issued for Ranchi, Khunti, Simdega, Gumla, Lohardaga, Saraikela-Kharsawan, East Singhbhum and West Singhbhum for 24 hours from 8.30 am on October 28. It focused on strengthening parliamentary institutions, the use of artificial intelligence and digital technologies and sustainability. The forum was held during India’s 2026 BRICS chairship, which had the theme “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability”. The joint declaration reaffirmed the principles of the United Nations Charter and called for comprehensive UN reform, including the Security Council, to make the international system “more just, equitable, democratic, representative, effective, and efficient”. “We look forward to strengthening BRICS interaction within international parliamentary fora, including the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU), to amplify the voice of the Global South,” the declaration said. The declaration also highlighted cooperation on emerging technologies including artificial intelligence and proposed a digital public infrastructure repository for BRICS countries. “We emphasise the need to strengthen the digital sovereignty of BRICS member countries by protecting data privacy and security of personal information as well as by building resilient national technological ecosystems,” it added. news.headline: 19-Month-Old Cheetah Cub Succumbs to Gunshot Wounds in Madhya Pradesh's Kuno National Park
news.story_lead: A 19-month-old male cheetah cub born to female cheetah Nirva died from gunshot injuries in Madhya Pradesh after being rescued from Morena district. Diagnostic scans revealed multiple firearm pellets lodged inside the cub's body, prompting the state government to form a Special Task Force to conduct a comprehensive investigation.
news.full_article_text:
### Incident Overview and Rescue Operation
A 19-month-old male cub of cheetah Nirva was rescued from the Pahargarh forest range in Morena district and brought to Kuno National Park for emergency care. Although initial reports suggested the animal had been beaten with sticks, subsequent veterinary examinations confirmed that the cheetah sustained fatal gunshot wounds.

### Medical Findings and Surgical Intervention
Diagnostic imaging performed at the Department of Veterinary Surgery and Radiology at NDVSU, Jabalpur, revealed several metallic objects within the animal's body:
- Pellets were detected near the lumbar (L1) and thoracic (T13) vertebrae, causing structural damage to the musculoskeletal and nervous systems.
- Two pellets were located in the subcutaneous tissues surrounding the left shoulder.
- One pellet was identified within the right lung parenchyma.
Veterinary surgeons extracted five firearm pellets during emergency surgery; however, the cub succumbed to its injuries on Tuesday morning.

### Circumstances Leading to the Event
According to local forest reports, the cub and another cheetah strayed into the outskirts of Bamori village in Morena, entering the courtyard of resident Somlavir Singh and killing two tethered calves. The noise alerted the family and other villagers. The injured cub was later found in the adjacent Pahargarh range. Authorities suspect the animal was shot either by a villager in retaliation or by poachers.

### Demographic Status and Institutional Response
- **Current Cheetah Population:** Following this death, India's total cheetah population stands at 58, distributed across Kuno National Park (52), Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary (4), and Veerangana Durgavati Tiger Reserve (2).
- **Government Investigation:** The Madhya Pradesh state government established a Special Task Force (STF) combining police and forest officers.
- **Demands for Independent Probe:** Wildlife activist Ajay Dubey called for a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe, criticizing existing surveillance arrangements managed by 18 tracking teams.

hindi_translation.story_lead: चीता निरवा के 19 महीने के नर शावक की मध्य प्रदेश के मुरैना जिले से रेस्क्यू किए जाने के बाद गोली लगने से मौत हो गई। मेडिकल स्कैन में शावक के शरीर में कई छर्रे पाए गए, जिसके बाद राज्य सरकार ने जांच के लिए विशेष कार्य बल (STF) का गठन किया है।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### घटना और बचाव अभियान
मादा चीता निरवा के 19 महीने के नर शावक को मुरैना जिले की पहाड़गढ़ रेंज से बचाकर इलाज के लिए कूनो राष्ट्रीय उद्यान लाया गया था। शुरुआती रिपोर्टों में लाठियों से चोट लगने की बात कही गई थी, लेकिन पशु चिकित्सा जांच में गोली लगने से घायल होने की पुष्टि हुई।

### चिकित्सीय निष्कर्ष और सर्जरी
जबलपुर स्थित NDVSU के पशु चिकित्सा सर्जरी एवं रेडियोलॉजी विभाग में किए गए सीटी स्कैन से शावक के शरीर में कई धातु के छर्रे मिले:
- रीढ़ की हड्डी (L1 और T13 वर्टेब्रा) के पास छर्रे पाए गए, जिससे तंत्रिका और मांसपेशी प्रणाली को गंभीर नुकसान पहुंचा।
- बाएं कंधे के पास त्वचा के नीचे दो छर्रे मिले।
- दाहिने फेफड़े के पैरेन्काइमा में एक छर्रा पाया गया।
आपतकालीन सर्जरी के दौरान पशु चिकित्सकों ने शरीर से पांच छर्रे निकाले, लेकिन मंगलवार सुबह शावक ने दम तोड़ दिया।

### घटना का कारण
स्थानीय वन अधिकारियों के अनुसार, यह शावक एक अन्य चीते के साथ मुरैना के बामोरी गांव की बाहरी सीमा में घुस गया था और एक घर के आंगन में बंधे दो बछड़ों का शिकार कर लिया। शोर सुनकर ग्रामीण एकत्र हो गए। बाद में शावक जंगल में घायल पाया गया। अंदेशा है कि ग्रामीणों या शिकारियों ने उस पर गोली चलाई।

### वर्तमान चीता आबादी और जांच
- **भारत में चीतों की संख्या:** इस घटना के बाद देश में कुल चीतों की संख्या 58 रह गई है, जिसमें कूनो राष्ट्रीय उद्यान में 52, गांधी सागर वन्यजीव अभयारण्य में 4 और वीरांगना दुर्गावती टाइगर रिजर्व में 2 चीते शामिल हैं।
- **सरकारी कार्रवाई:** राज्य सरकार ने पुलिस और वन अधिकारियों को मिलाकर एक विशेष कार्य बल (STF) गठित किया है।
- **CBI जांच की मांग:** वन्यजीव कार्यकर्ता अजय दुबे ने 18 निगरानी टीमों के बावजूद सुरक्षा में हुई चूक को लेकर सीबीआई जांच की मांग की है।
